title: Per-account regression sentinel with private probe runners and policy-bound telemetry
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a per-account regression sentinel that runs customer-scoped probe suites inside customer-owned private contexts (VPC or on-prem probe runners) and emits policy-bound, minimal telemetry to Redwood’s control plane for gating rollouts and model/config changes. The goal is to detect quality regressions tied to model builds or config flips before global rollouts, while preserving customer data isolation and complying with enterprise privacy controls.

Background: Customers on Dedicated and Private deployments have asked for a way to run their own golden prompts/acceptance checks as part of our model/config rollout pipeline without shipping PII or raw prompts to Redwood. Existing org-scoped evals send telemetry to our central eval pipeline; this work proposes a hybrid model: lightweight private probe runners under customer control, local scoring against small golden sets, and hashed/aggregated signals sent back for gating decisions.

Goals:
- Provide an out-of-the-box per-account canary gate that evaluates candidate model/config changes on customer-specific probe suites.
- Ensure no raw customer prompts, completions, or embeddings leave the customer VPC by default. Only minimal, policy-approved digests (hashes, aggregated metrics, anonymized failure categories) may be sent.
- Integrate with rollout policies (canary size, failure budget, auto-rollback) in Console so product teams can opt into account-scoped gating.
- Support both Hosted Dedicated (Redwood-managed but tenant-isolated) and Private (customer-managed) deployments with the same developer ergonomics.
- Provide clear opt-in UX and compliance artifacts for SOC/ISO customers.

Scope & Non‑Goals:
In scope: private probe runner agent (lightweight container), control-plane orchestration hooks (job scheduling, timeout, retry), telemetry schema with strict allowlist, console UI for per-account probe management, rollout integration, acceptance criteria, and docs.
Out of scope: building full local human-in-the-loop review tooling, full federation of golden-set updates (customers can upload sets manually or via API), automated differential privacy transformations beyond hashing/aggregation.

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- Local vs central eval: Local runners preserve privacy but increase operational surface and customer onboarding complexity. We mitigate by providing a one-click installer and a hosted-managed runner option for Dedicated customers where allowable.
- Telemetry minimalism: We will limit outbound telemetry to preapproved fields (probe_id, pass_rate_bucket, regression_delta_bucket, model_id, timestamp, opt-in token). This minimizes leakage but reduces signal fidelity; acceptance thresholds will account for noisier signals.
- Cost: Running per-account probes increases compute; we propose configurable cadence and sample size (default: 5 probes, daily for canary) with overridable limits per contract.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Customers can register a probe suite via Console or API and choose execution mode: customer-managed runner (required for highest isolation) or Redwood-managed tenant-isolated runner (available for Dedicated).
2) A candidate model/config rollout triggers per-account probes for accounts that have opted into the gate.
3) Local runner executes probes against the candidate and baseline, computes allowed aggregated metrics, and posts only the allowlisted telemetry to control plane.
4) Control plane evaluates telemetry against per-account thresholds; failures increment the account’s failure budget and can trigger automatic rollback or manual review according to rollout policy.
5) End-to-end test coverage: functional tests in our e2e harness plus a sample Private customer deployment in CI.
6) Documentation and compliance pack ready for SOC review.

Telemetry & dataflow (high level):
- Probe-runner executes locally. Raw artifacts (prompts, completions) are stored only in customer environment.
- Runner computes: pass_rate (binned), semantic_delta_estimate (binned), and a cryptographic hash of the prompt id + goldenset id (one-way).
- Runner sends: {model_id, probe_suite_id_hash, pass_rate_bucket, regression_delta_bucket, execution_timestamp, runner_manifest_version}.
- Control plane maps hashed probe suite id to customer account and evaluates gate. No raw text is persisted centrally.

Operational notes:
- Default cadence: on every model major/minor version promotion to canary and on config changes that affect decoding/temperature/quantization profile.
- Time budget per probe-runner job: default 300s; job backoff and alerting required.
- Metrics surfaced in Console: per-account gate pass/fail, historical trend, sample size, and recent failing prompts count (as counts only, not the text).

Open questions:
- Do enterprise customers want optional hashed completion fingerprints for stronger regression matching? (privacy vs fidelity trade-off)
- Should we implement an encrypted telemetry relay for Private customers who do not want any telemetry hitting Redwood control plane unencrypted?

Risks:
- Misconfiguration by customers could produce false positives/negatives; mitigate with clear defaults and sanity checks.
- Legal/regulatory: some customers require zero outbound signal. We will provide an explicit ‘no-telemetry’ mode which disables remote gating and surfaces only local reports.

Next steps:
- Finalize telemetry allowlist with Security and Legal.
- RFC for runner architecture (lightweight container vs systemd agent) and onboarding UX.
- Align ENG workload and schedule prototype spike (2 sprints) to validate end-to-end latency, cost, and signal quality.
comments: 2026-02-12: Initial scoping meeting with Eng (Ravi, Mei), Security (Jordan), and Legal (Priya). Consensus: require allowlist telemetry and offer a no-telemetry mode for high-compliance tenants.
2026-02-18: Design doc draft uploaded to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/pm/PM-63412-runner-design (private). Asked Eng to evaluate container vs agent trade-offs in spike.
2026-02-25: Eng spike (ENG-28913) started. Spike goals: run a minimal probe suite in a mock VPC with hashed telemetry to control plane; measure job latency and cost for 50 simulated accounts.

2026-03-03: Spike results: median probe run 1.8s per prompt, full suite (5 probes) ~12s; estimated cost per account per run (gcpu equivalent) ~ $0.006. Findings in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/probes/pull/142

2026-03-05: Security reviewed telemetry proposal; asked to remove any stable identifiers and to add rotating opt-in tokens. Security suggested cryptographic salt in hashes. Marked as required before rollout.
2026-03-08: UX sketch review with Design (Lina) — console flow for enabling per-account probes and viewing gate history approved pending accessibility tweaks.

2026-03-10: Meeting with Sales/CS to map contractual limits for Dedicated customers. Decision: Dedicated tenants can choose Redwood-managed tenant-isolated runners if contract permits; Private customers default to customer-managed runners.
2026-03-11: Blocker identified: some on-prem customers run air-gapped environments with no outbound connectivity. Action: implement 'local-only' mode and document differences in gating behavior.
2026-03-12: Next engineering milestone: integration PR for control-plane gating API (ENG-50102) scheduled for review 2026-03-18. PM to coordinate acceptance criteria with QA.
2026-03-15: Plan to schedule a pilot with 3 dedicated customers for April; prepare pilot onboarding checklist and security questionnaire.
